findingDetails.title: A Claude transcript row larger than the 256 KiB tail silently suppresses the nudge

focus: correctness: shared usage and threshold-to-nudge path

searchLedger.hypothesis: A final assistant record larger than the configured tail can be clipped and rejected, suppressing the Claude nudge.
searchLedger.invariant: The newest main-chain assistant usage must remain readable when the transcript exceeds the tail window.
searchLedger.rationale: The truncated final row is discarded, and the Claude adapter has an explicit quiet return on null usage.

searchActions.result: The reader starts at size minus 262144 bytes, drops a malformed first fragment, and returns null when no complete assistant row remains.
A null usage result returns done without running the threshold decision.
Existing long-transcript coverage places a complete final row inside the configured tail; no oversized-row case is covered.
Earlier review material covered dropping an initial partial line, but no matching active oversized-final-row finding was located; this residual remains in current code.

focus: correctness: suppression guards, nudge reminders, and adapter delivery

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Shared suppression rules plus five adapter delivery paths feed the automatic hop.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A shared guard could suppress a required reminder or allow a nudge outside the relaunch loop.
searchLedger.invariant: Every adapter should apply the same loop, pending handoff, hop-cap, and nudge-level guards.
searchLedger.rationale: The reviewed shared ordering matches the intended suppressions; the adapters invoke the shared decision before emitting handoff text.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No divergence found in the shared guard order.

searchActions.result: All five automatic runtimes call the shared decision; it checks threshold, loop presence, a live handoff, hop cap, then the current level.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A threshold-crossing Pi message could be consumed by prepare before the reminder is delivered.
searchLedger.invariant: Pi must delay the nudge until agent_end and discard it if the event already created a pending or armed record.
searchLedger.rationale: The delayed delivery path rechecks the exact conditions that could make the held nudge redundant.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No lost or prematurely emitted held nudge was found in the current path.

searchActions.result: Pi stores the nudge by session, attempts arming at agent_end, retires text for a live record or hop cap, and otherwise sends a follow-up that triggers a turn.

searchLedger.hypothesis: OpenCode may lose its first nudge on host restart or deliver the +5% reminder before the first prompt.
searchLedger.invariant: OpenCode should persist the delivered level and replay an undelivered first nudge after a host restart.
searchLedger.rationale: The source preserves the level across the delivery boundary and its shared boundary logic is covered.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No lost first reminder or incorrect +5% boundary was identified.

searchActions.result: OpenCode queues at threshold, keeps a local level, replays a persisted spent level only when no active nudge exists, and persists the level when consuming the pending output.
Shared tests cover exact threshold, threshold plus five points, one-shot behavior, and persisted level handling.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A fresh armed record with a future timestamp could be treated as pending forever after a backward clock adjustment.
searchLedger.invariant: A clock-reversed armed record must not suppress the next useful nudge.
searchLedger.rationale: Adversarially rechecked prior finding DS-009 against current code.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The reviewed condition is fixed in current shouldRelaunch.

searchActions.result: Current shouldRelaunch treats now earlier than armedAt as stale; handoffPending suppresses an armed record only while armedRecordStillCurrent says it is fresh.
The earlier report recorded this issue; current source has the future-timestamp stale guard, so it is not a current finding.

deferred: Claude hook registration and event binding

searchLedger.hypothesis: An adapter may arm a record belonging to another loop, session, or runtime, or accept an unrelated event.
searchLedger.invariant: Only the matching loop/session/runtime and intended host event may arm this record.
searchLedger.rationale: The shared identity gate refuses mismatched loop/session/runtime and adapter handlers are bound to their host event; Claude registration itself is deferred for direct config verification.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No mismatched record was found in the reviewed event paths.

searchActions.result: The shared guard checks loopId, sessionId, runtime, status, and live-killer ownership; Codex and Hermes match named events, while Pi and OpenCode enter through their host event handlers.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A repeated arm event may spawn a redundant killer for a record that already has a live killer.
searchLedger.invariant: An already-armed record may be re-armed only after its killer lock is gone.
searchLedger.rationale: Current shared guard checks status plus liveKillerPid before re-arming.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The current code rejects an already-armed record while a killer owns the lock.

searchActions.result: armableRecord rejects non-pending status while the live killer lock exists; the archived Claude omission is fixed by the current shared guard.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A first killer spawn error may leave the runtime alive with an armed record and no supervisor to signal it.
searchLedger.invariant: A failed killer launch must not leave an interactive automatic hop waiting indefinitely for the runtime to exit.
searchLedger.rationale: A one-time spawn error has no self-retry, and the wrapper cannot evaluate the armed record until the interactive runtime has exited.

searchActions.queryOrPath: four interactive arm handlers and killer startup
searchActions.result: Each logs spawn failure but leaves the record armed; no immediate retry is scheduled.

searchActions.queryOrPath: adapter spawn-error tests and archived review reports
searchActions.result: Current tests assert the armed record remains on spawn errors. Prior reports only cover duplicate Claude arm and other killer concerns, not retry after initial spawn failure.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Re-arming after a dead killer may preserve an old timestamp or cwd, causing the wrapper to reject the replacement killer's record.
searchLedger.invariant: A replacement killer must supervise a record with a fresh armedAt and current cwd.
searchLedger.rationale: The shared transition restamps both fields, and current tests cover the core behavior plus a runtime adapter.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The stale timestamp/cwd failure fixed in phase 011 does not remain in current arm logic.

searchActions.result: arm restamps armedAt and cwd, and the core test asserts both persisted values change on re-arm.
Pi adapter test confirms an old armed record is re-armed with live cwd so the wrapper will relaunch.

findingDetails.title: timeout cleanup can disarm a newer armed record for the same handoff path

focus: traceability: killer idle, signal, grace, timeout, and record-change behavior

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: The race crosses prepare, shared record state, two killer lock owners, timeout cleanup, and the wrapper wait loop.

deferred: full hook registration and linked repository state resolution

searchLedger.hypothesis: A missing or changing transcript can make the killer signal too early or fail to time out.
searchLedger.invariant: The killer waits for the idle interval and a missing transcript grace before signaling.
searchLedger.rationale: The current wait loop enforces idle and missing-file grace before the signal path.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No early-signal path was found in the reviewed branch.

searchActions.result: Transcript changes reset idle tracking; one missing stat is tolerated, and persistent absence returns through timeout.

searchLedger.hypothesis: An older killer may disarm or notify for a newer record after its wait expires.
searchLedger.invariant: Timeout cleanup may mutate only the record the killer observed.
searchLedger.rationale: Path equality does not distinguish a newer record when it reuses the same handoff file.

searchActions.result: The timeout re-reads and compares handoff paths, then unarms by status and handoff path.
A different-path replacement is covered and remains armed after the old killer times out.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A repeated prepare for the same note may be overwritten and later disarmed by a stale killer.
searchLedger.invariant: A replacement prepared record must survive timeout cleanup from a prior killer.
searchLedger.rationale: An old killer can disarm a same-path replacement after its replacement killer loses lock ownership.

searchActions.result: preparePending overwrites the loop record; pending is armable even while the previous killer owns the lock.
The new killer exits on the live lock; the old killer compares only the path and can unarm the replacement record.
The same-path re-prepare test leaves the replacement pending; it does not re-arm it before the old timeout.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The killer may signal a target outside the loop or fail to honor the shutdown grace period.
searchLedger.invariant: Signal only a live loop descendant after hop/freshness checks and then wait the full grace interval.
searchLedger.rationale: The target gates and post-signal grace are present.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No signal/grace ordering defect was found.

searchActions.result: Before SIGTERM the killer checks cap, freshness, liveness, and ancestry; after SIGTERM it starts a fresh signal grace.
